                "headline": "Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 2:19AM EDT until October 11 at 5:15AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC",
                "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Cherokee County in upstate South Carolina...\n\n* WHEN...Until 515 AM EDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams\nand other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,\ngreenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and\nparking lots. Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible. A\nfew flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible. A small\nculvert washout or two is possible.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 218 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a line of torrential\nrainfall has just recently departed Cherokee County, with\nadditional cells of moderate rainfall moving into the county from\nthe south.  This rainfall is occurring on top of saturated soils\ndue to a prolonged period of light to moderate showers that have\noccurred over the county since yesterday morning.  Widespread,\nstorm-total rainfall of the 2.5-3.5 inches fell yesterday. The\nrainfall has accumulated steadily, allowing soils to slowly\nsaturate and runoff to slowly increase, resulting in steady rises\nin small streams. However, this brief period of torrential\nrainfall may cause more rapid rises to develop, especially near\nChesnee in the headwaters of Thicketty Creek, Zekial Creek,\nLittle Horse Creek, and Suck Creek as well as in city of Gaffney\nat the headwaters of Peoples Creek, Limestone Creek, and Irene\nCreek.  Isolated out-of-bank conditions impacting low-lying areas\nadjacent to streams are likely to develop over the next 1-3\nhours.\n\n- Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms may develop\nbetween 4am and 9am this morning.  These showers and storms will\nbe very efficient at producing heavy rainfall.  Soils are\nsaturated and streams are swollen. Therefore, additional heavy\nrain may quickly create new areas of flooding and cause previous\nareas of flooding to redevelop.  As a result, Flash Flood\nWarnings may be issued tonight.  Caution is advised near any\nstream or other vulnerable area.  Seek higher ground immediately\nif heavy rain develops.  Please have a plan in place should flash\nflooding develop and do not hesitate to act.  Please heed all\nevacuation orders from Emergency Management officials.\n\n- Some locations that may experience flooding include...\nGaffney, Cowpens, Blacksburg, Pacolet Mills, Grover, Cowpens\nNational Battlefield, Kings Mountain State Park, Crowders\nMountain State Park, Draytonville and Cherokee Falls.\n- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
                "instruction": "Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.",

                "headline": "Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 2:10AM EDT until October 11 at 6:30AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC",
                "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.\n\n* WHERE...Northwestern Caldwell County in western North Carolina...\n\n* WHEN...Until 630 AM EDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams\nand other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,\ngreenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and\nparking lots.  Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible. A\nfew flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A\nsmall culvert washout or two is possible.\n\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 203 AM EDT, Light to moderate showers continue to move from\nsouth to north across the northern Blue Ridge escarpment and\nvicinity, with heavier showers approaching from the south.\nRainfall of the 2-4 inches have fallen over the past 12 hours.\nThe rainfall has accumulated steadily, allowing soils to slowly\nsaturate and runoff to slowly increase, resulting in steady rises\nin area streams including the Yadkin River, Johns River, Mulberry\nCreek and Buffalo Creek.\n\n- Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms are expected to\ndevelop over the next few hours and the threat will persist\nthrough the early morning hours on Sunday.  These showers and\nstorms will be very efficient at producing heavy rainfall. Soils\nare saturated and streams are swollen. Therefore, additional\nheavy rain may quickly create new areas of flooding and cause\nprevious areas of flooding to redevelop.  As a result, Flash\nFlood Warnings may be issued tonight.  Caution is advised near\nany stream or other vulnerable area.  Seek higher ground\nimmediately if heavy rain develops.  Please have a plan in place\nshould flash flooding develop and do not hesitate to act. Please\nheed all evacuation orders from Emergency Management officials.\n\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nBlowing Rock In Caldwell County, Grandfather Mountain State Park,\nB.R. Parkway-Linville Falls To Grandfather, Patterson, Upton,\nGlobe and Collettsville.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
                "instruction": "Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.",

                "description": "FFWGSP\n\nThe National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has extended\nthe\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nSoutheastern Avery County in western North Carolina...\nNorthwestern Burke County in western North Carolina...\nWest Central Caldwell County in western North Carolina...\n\n* Until 400 AM EDT.\n\n* At 139 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the warned\narea.                 "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, including the following\nareas, Hualapai Mountains, Lake Havasu and Fort Mohave, Lake Mead -\nAZ side, Lake Mohave - AZ side, Northwest Deserts and Northwest\nPlateau, southeast California, including the following areas, Cadiz\nBasin, Death Valley National Park, Eastern Mojave Desert, Morongo\nBasin, San Bernardino County-Upper Colorado River Valley and\nWestern Mojave Desert, and Nevada, including the following areas,\nEsmeralda and Central Nye County, Lake Mead - NV side, Lake Mohave\n- NV side, Las Vegas Valley, Lincoln County, Northeast Clark\nCounty, Sheep Range, Southern Clark County, Spring Mountains-Red\nRock Canyon and Western Clark and Southern Nye County.\n\n* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nFlooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.                 "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
                "senderName": "NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC",
                "headline": "Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 12:24AM EDT until October 11 at 6:15AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC",
                "description": "FFWGSP\n\nThe National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nBurke County in western North Carolina...\n\n* Until 615 AM EDT.\n\n* At 1224 AM EDT, Earlier today, a prolonged period of steady\nrainfall produced 3-6 inches across Burke County, saturating area\nsoils.  Doppler radar shows several rounds of torrential rainfall\nhave moved through the area from the south, capable of producing\n1.5-3 inches of rainfall on top of saturated soils.  This rainfall\nwill cause new areas of Minor flooding to develop.\n\n* Areas of greatest concern include along Hunting Creek near\nMorganton; poorly draining areas of Morganton and other urban areas\nalong US 70; Silver Creek south of Glen Alpine; and Henry and Jacob\nforks of the South Fork Catawba River near South Mountains State\nPark.\n\n* Additional areas of Minor Flooding are expected to develop over the\nnext 1-3 hours.  Please obey all barricades and heed all evacuation\norders from local Emergency Management officials.  Only 12 inches\nof water can strand your vehicle or sweep it away.\n\nHAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.\n\nSOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.\n\nIMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,\nincluding parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat- access\nareas, and campgrounds.  Significant flooding of\npoor-drainage areas are likely, impacting travel.\nLow-lying roadways are likely to be flooded, requiring\nbarricades.\n\n* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...\nMorganton, Longview, Valdese, Salem, Icard, Drexel, Hildebran,\nConnelly Springs, Rutherford College and Glen Alpine.",
                "instruction": "Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.",

                "description": "...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in North\nCarolina...\n\nFrench Broad River at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W Fletcher affecting\nBuncombe and Henderson Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.\n\n* WHERE...French Broad River near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W\nFletcher.\n\n* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Action Stage continues.                 "description": "FFWGSP\n\nThe National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nHenderson County in western North Carolina...\nPolk County in western North Carolina...\nEastern Transylvania County in western North Carolina...\n\n* Until 515 AM EDT.\n\n* At 1116 PM EDT, Earlier today, a prolonged period of steady\nrainfall produced 3-6 inches across eastern Transylvania,\nHenderson, and Polk counties, saturating area soils and causing\nscattered areas of nuisance flooding.  Doppler radar shows several\nrounds of torrential rainfall has moved through the area from the\nsouth, capable of producing 2-3 inches of rainfall on top of\nsaturated soils.  This rainfall will exacerbate areas of ongoing\nnuisance flooding and cause new areas of Minor flooding to develop.\n\n* Areas of greatest concern include along the Little River from Cedar\nMountain to Penrose; the Davidson River near Pisgah Forest; the\nFrench Broad River from Brevard to Mills River; Mud Creek from Crab\nCreek to Hendersonville to Mountain Home; White Oak Creek from Mill\nSpring to Green Creek; and Boylston Creek near Forge Mountain.\n\n* Additional areas of Minor Flooding are expected to develop over the\nnext 1-3 hours.  Please obey all barricades and heed all evacuation\norders from local Emergency Management officials.  Only a few\ninches of water can strand your vehicle and only 6 inches of water\ncan sweep your vehicle away.\n\nHAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,\nincluding parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat- access\nareas, and campgrounds.  Significant flooding of\npoor-drainage areas are likely, impacting travel.\nLow-lying roadways are likely to be flooded, requiring\nbarricades.   An isolated landslide or two cannot be ruled\nout.\n\n* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...\nHendersonville, Brevard, Columbus, Mills River, Fletcher, Flat\nRock, Etowah, Mountain Home, Laurel Park and Tryon.",
                "instruction": "Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.\n\nThe additional heavy rain will increase the risk of landslides and\ndebris flows, especially in areas where landslides have occurred in\nthe past.                 "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Southwestern Avery County in western North Carolina...\nSoutheastern Mitchell County in western North Carolina...\nSoutheastern Yancey County in western North Carolina...\n\n* WHEN...Until 500 AM EDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams\nand other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,\ngreenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and\nparking lots.                 "event": "Tropical Cyclone Local Statement",
                "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
                "senderName": "NWS San Diego CA",
                "headline": "Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 10 at 8:11PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA",
                "description": "HLSSGX\n\nThis product covers EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA\n\n**Impacts from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel Expected in San Diego\nCounty Late Tonight through Early Sunday Afternoon**\n\nNEW INFORMATION\n---------------\n\n* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:\n- None\n\n* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:\n- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for San Diego County\nCoastal Areas, San Diego County Deserts, San Diego County\nMountains, and San Diego County Valleys\n\n* STORM INFORMATION:\n- About 240 miles south-southeast of San Mateo Point CA or about\n180 miles south-southeast of Mouth of Tijuana River CA\n- 30.0N 116.5W\n- Storm Intensity 60 mph\n- Movement North-northeast or 15 degrees at 36 mph\n\nSITUATION OVERVIEW\n------------------\n\nImpacts from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel Expected in San Diego County\nLate Tonight through Early Sunday Afternoon.\n\nPost-Tropical Cyclone Rachel is currently about 190 miles south of San\nDiego, moving north-northeast towards Northern Baja at about 36 mph.\nRachel is expected to make landfall south of the US/Mexico Border\ntonight. Though Rachel no longer has tropical characteristics,\ntropical storm level impacts will likely affect San Diego County. A\nTropical Storm Watch remains in effect for all of San Diego County.\nThe main concerns with Tropical Storm Rachel are coastal flooding,\nwind, and periods of heavy rain which could lead to localized flooding\nand flash flooding. The majority of impacts from the tropical storm\nare expected late tonight through early Sunday afternoon.\n\nSouth swell from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel will arrive on Sunday.\nThe combination of south and northwest swells, increased onshore\nwinds, and high tides over 7 feet will maintain a threat of coastal\nflooding and beach erosion along area beaches. Surf on Sunday is\ncurrently expected to peak at 6 to 9 feet, decreasing to 3 to 6 feet\nfor Monday and Tuesday. Confidence in impactful coastal flooding is\nhigh, with significant coastal flooding and beach erosion likely.\n\nWidespread rain is expected late tonight into late Sunday morning from\nPost-Tropical Cyclone Rachel. There is expected to be a gradient in\nrainfall amounts with the higher amounts over San Diego County, the\nmountains, and parts of the low desert. Peak rainfall rates of 0.50 to\n0.60 inches are possible for the coast and valleys, 0.50 to\n0.70 inches per hour possible for the deserts, and 0.70 to 1 inch per\nhour for the mountains. Current forecast has rainfall totals of\n0.50 to 1.25 inches for the coast, valleys, and deserts and 1 to\n2.5 inches for the mountains. Areas of flash and urban flooding are\nprobable, especially where the maximum rainfall rates occur. The San\nDiego River at Fashion Valley is currently forecast to crest at\n8.1 feet (action/monitor stage) just before noon on Sunday. Those with\ninterests near the San Diego River should continue to monitor the\nforecast.\n\nIncreased winds are expected with the onset and passage of\nPost-Tropical Cyclone Rachel. Sustained winds of 39+ mph are expected\non the southeast side of the storm. Based on the current track, more\nsouthern and eastern parts of San Diego County are most likely to see\nwinds of this magnitude. Regardless, strong sustained winds and wind\ngusts can be expected on Sunday. Winds will likely be enhanced by\nlocal terrain with gusts 40 to 55 mph on the desert slopes of the\nmountains and into the deserts. Local gusts up to 60 mph possible on\nmountain ridges and in passes and canyons. Winds are expected to\nremain elevated in Rachel's wake with continued strong gusts on the\ndesert mountain slopes into the deserts through Monday morning.\n\nPOTENTIAL IMPACTS\n-----------------\n\n* WIND:\nPrepare for hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across\nEXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA. Potential impacts in this area\ninclude:\n- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored\nmobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.\n- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or\nuprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are\nshallow rooted, especially in coastal and valley locations that\ndon't typically experience strong winds. Some fences and\nroadway signs blown over.\n- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban\nor heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on\nbridges and other elevated roadways.\n- Scattered power and communications outages.\n\nElsewhere across EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA, little to no impact\nis anticipated.\n\n\n* FLOODING RAIN:\nPrepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible\nextensive impacts across San Diego County. Potential impacts include:\n- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.\n- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in\nmultiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, arroyos, and\nditches may become dangerous rivers. In mountain areas,\ndestructive runoff may run quickly down valleys while\nincreasing susceptibility to rockslides and mudslides. Flood\ncontrol systems and barriers may become stressed.\n- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple\ncommunities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed\naway. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.\nStreets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with\nunderpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.\nMany road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.\n\nPrepare for dangerous rainfall flooding having possible significant\nimpacts across San Diego County.\n\n* OTHER COASTAL HAZARDS:\n- High tides over 7 ft, combined with high surf and gusty onshore\nwinds will increase the threat for coastal flooding across area\nbeaches. Additionally surf of 6 to 9 ft will create dangerous swimming\nconditions. Significant coastal flooding and beach erosion is\nlikely.\n\n\nPRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS\n----------------------------------\n\n* EVACUATIONS:\nFollow the advice of local officials.\n\n* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:\nIf you live in a place particularly vulnerable to flooding, such as\nnear the ocean, in a low-lying or poor drainage area, in a valley, or\nnear a river, plan to move to safe shelter on higher ground.\n\nAlways heed the advice of local officials and comply with orders that\nare issued. Do not needlessly jeopardize your life or the lives of\nothers.\n\nClosely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather Radio and local news\noutlets for official storm information. Listen for possible changes\nto the forecast.\n\n* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:\n- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov\n- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org\n- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org\n\nNEXT UPDATE\n-----------\n\nThe next local statement will be issued by the National Weather\nService in San Diego CA around 2 AM PDT, or sooner if conditions\nwarrant.",

                "description": "* LOCATIONS AFFECTED\n- Oceanside\n- Carlsbad\n- Chula Vista\n- San Diego\n\n* WIND\n- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Below tropical storm force wind\n- Peak Wind Forecast: 10-20 mph with gusts to 30 mph\n\n- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST\nUNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for wind 39\nto 57 mph\n- The wind threat has remained nearly steady from the\nprevious assessment.\n- PLAN: Plan for hazardous wind of equivalent tropical storm\nforce.\n- PREPARE: Efforts to protect property should now be\nunderway.                 "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
                "senderName": "NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC",
                "headline": "Flash Flood Warning issued October 10 at 10:50PM EDT until October 11 at 4:30AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC",
                "description": "FFWGSP\n\nThe National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nSpartanburg County in upstate South Carolina...\n\n* Until 430 AM EDT.\n\n* At 1050 PM EDT, Earlier today, a prolonged period of steady\nrainfall produced 2.5-4 inches across Spartanburg County,\nsaturating area soils and causing isolated areas of nuisance\nflooding.  Doppler radar shows an axis of torrential rainfall has\nmoved into Spartanburg County from the south, capable of producing\n1-2 inches of rainfall on top of saturated soils.  This rainfall\nwill exacerbate areas of ongoing nuisance flooding and cause new\nareas of flooding to develop. The heaviest rainfall is currently\nimpacting Cross Anchor, Enoree, and Pauiine.\n\n* Areas of greatest concern include along Lawsons Fork Creek and\nMeadow Creek near Inman; the South Pacolet River, Motlow Creek, and\nHolston Creek near Campobello; Bear Creek and Obed Creek north of\nLake Bowen; and areas near Croft State Park.  Earlier, Glendale\nFire Department reported nuisance flooding along Country Club Rd\nnear Church St.  Flood conditions there are likely to worsen.\nPlease obey all barricades and avoid flooded roadways.  Only a few\ninches of water can strand your vehicle.\n\n* Additional areas of Minor Flooding are expected to develop over the\nnext 1-3 hours.  Please obey all barricades and heed all evacuation\norders from local Emergency Management officials.\n\nHAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,\nincluding  parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat-\naccess areas, and  campgrounds.  Significant flooding of\npoor-drainage areas are likely, impacting travel.\nLow-lying roadways are likely to be flooded, requiring\nbarricades.\n\n* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...\nSpartanburg, Boiling Springs SC, Woodruff, Lyman, Pacolet, Cowpens,\nWellford, Inman, Mayo and Roebuck.",
                "instruction": "Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.",

                "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...In Northeast Georgia, the following counties: Elbert,\nFranklin, Habersham, Hart, Rabun and Stephens. In western North\nCarolina, the following counties: Avery, Buncombe, Burke, Caldwell,\nMcDowell, Polk,  Rutherford, Haywood, Henderson, Macon, Mitchell,\nJackson, Transylvania and Yancey. In Upstate South Carolina, the\nfollowing counties: Abbeville, Anderson, Central Greenville,\nGreater Oconee, Greater Pickens, Greenville, Greenwood, Laurens,\nSpartanburg, and Oconee.\n\n* WHEN...Through Sunday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nCreeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings\nmay be flooded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- As the remnants of Isaias move northward into the lower Ohio\nValley, periods of rain will continue. High rainfall rates will\ncontinue in short bursts through the overnight hours. By Sunday\nmorning, total accumulations of generally 5 to 8 inches are\nexpected along the southeast-facing Blue Ridge Escarpment, with 2\nto 5 inches elsewhere in the watch area.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
                "instruction": "A Flood Watch for flash flooding means there is a potential for rapid\nonset flooding based on current forecasts. Flash flooding is a very\ndangerous situation and may impact areas that do not typically flood.\nPlease monitor the latest forecasts and be prepared to take action\nquickly should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.\n\nRainfall of more than five inches in similar storms has been\nassociated with an increased risk of landslides, especially\nfast-moving debris flows and debris slides. If you live on a\nmountainside or in a cove at the base of a mountain, especially near\na stream, be ready to leave in advance of the storm and follow\nevacuation orders from local officials. Consider postponing travel\nalong mountain roads during the heavy rainfall event.",

                "description": "FFWGSP\n\nThe National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nRutherford County in western North Carolina...\n\n* Until 445 AM EDT Sunday.\n\n* At 1039 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing\nheavy rain across the warned area. Seek higher ground immediately if heavy rain\ndevelops. Please have a plan in place should you experience flash\nflooding and do not hesitate to act.  Please heed all evacuation\norders from Emergency Management officials.",

                "senderName": "NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC",
                "headline": "Flood Watch issued October 10 at 10:30PM EDT until October 12 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC",
                "description": "Moderate to heavy rainfall is expected as the remnants of Isaias\ntrack across the region starting early Sunday morning. Storms should\nbe highly efficient rainfall producers given the tropical nature of\nthe air mass. In particular, the eastern slopes of the Blue Ridge\nhave the potential to see the most rainfall given the continued\neasterly upslope winds. A further eastward expansion of these watches\nmay be needed.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, northern, and northwest Virginia,\nincluding the following areas, in central Virginia, Albemarle,\nCentral Virginia Blue Ridge, Greene, Nelson and Orange. In northern\nVirginia, Culpeper, Northern Fauquier and Southern Fauquier. In\nnorthwest Virginia, Madison, Northern Virginia Blue Ridge and\nRappahannock.\n\n* WHEN...From 5 AM EDT Sunday through late Sunday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- The remnants of Isaias will bring a tropical air mass much into\nthe Mid-Atlantic region late tonight into Sunday. Storms should\nbe highly efficient in this environment and capable of producing\nseveral inches of rain throughout the duration of the event.\nStorm total rainfall is expected to be around 2 to 3 inches, with\npockets of 3 to 5 inches along the eastern slopes of the Blue\nRidge.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

                "headline": "Flash Flood Warning issued October 10 at 10:25PM EDT until October 11 at 4:15AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC",
                "description": "FFWGSP\n\nThe National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nMcDowell County in western North Carolina...\n\n* Until 415 AM EDT.\n\n* At 1025 PM EDT, Rounds of torrential rainfall have impacted many\nareas of McDowell County following a prolonged period of steady\nlight to moderate rain, which produced storm-total rainfall of 2-4\ninches over the past 12 hours.  Unfortunately, this current\ntorrential rainfall is producing another 1.5-2.5 inches of rain\nover the past couple of hours.  This rainfall over saturated soils\nis causing more significant rises to develop along areas streams\nand associated tributaries.  Areas of greatest concern include the\nheadwaters of Cove Creek and the Second Broad River near Sugar\nHill, where the 3300 block of Sugar Hill Road is closed due to\nflooding; Nix Creek near Providence; Crooked Creek near Moffitt\nHill; and the Upper Catawba River between Old Fort and Pleasant\nGardens, including along Lytle Mountain Rd, where a foot of flood\nwaters have currently closed the roadway.  Additionally, a\nlandslide has been observed on NC-226A with minor impacts to the\nroadway.  Additional areas of Minor flooding are expected to\ndevelop over the next 1-3 hours.  Please obey all barricades and\nheed all evacuation orders from local Emergency Management\nofficials.\n\nHAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,\nincluding  parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat-\naccess areas, and campgrounds.  Low-lying roadways are\nlikely to be flooded.                 "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...\nAlabama...Georgia...\n\nShoal River near Mossy Head (CR 1087) affecting Walton County.\n\nChoctawhatchee River at Geneva (SR 52) affecting Geneva County.\n\nOchlockonee River near Thomasville (US 84) affecting Thomas and\nGrady Counties.\n\n...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nAlabama...Florida...\n\nPea River near Ariton (US 231) affecting Coffee and Dale Counties.\n\nChoctawhatchee River near Caryville (US 90) affecting Washington\nand Holmes Counties.\n\n...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in\nAlabama...Florida...\n\nPea River at Elba (US 84) affecting Coffee County.\n\nSt. Marks River near Newport On Old Magnolia Rd affecting Leon and\nWakulla Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pea River near Ariton (US 231).\n\n* WHEN...Until Tuesday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, The backyard of a home near U.S. Highway\n231 and Pea River will start to flood.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:00 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 8.6 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 14.0 feet\nTuesday morning.\n- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 13.9\nfeet on 02/20/1942.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

                "senderName": "NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC",
                "headline": "Flash Flood Warning issued October 10 at 10:08PM EDT until October 11 at 4:15AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC",
                "description": "FFWGSP\n\nThe National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nSoutheastern Buncombe County in western North Carolina...\nNortheastern Henderson County in western North Carolina...\nNorthwestern Rutherford County in western North Carolina...\n\n* Until 415 AM EDT Sunday.\n\n* At 1008 PM EDT, Rounds of torrential rainfall have impacted the\nupper Broad/Rocky Broad River watershed, including over Lake Lure.\nStorm-total rainfall of the 3-4 inches have fallen over the past 12\nhours prior to this torrential rainfall, but another 1-2 inches of\nrain have fallen over the past couple of hours.  This rainfall over\nsaturated soils is causing more significant rises to develop along\nthe Rocky Broad River and associated tributaries.  The streamgauge\non the Rocky Broad River near Bat Cave has just exceeded Minor\nFlood Stage of 7.5 feet and is expected to continue to rise to\n8-8.5 feet before slowing or cresting.  High flows along the Rocky\nBroad River into Chimney Rock will result in flooding of US 64/74\n(Main St) near Dogwood RV Park.  Additional areas of Minor flooding\nare expected to develop over the next 1-2 hours.  Please obey all\nbarricades and heed all evacuation orders from local Emergency\nManagement officials.\n\nHAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,\nincluding  parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat-\naccess areas, and  campgrounds.  Low-lying roadways are\nlikely to be flooded.  An  isolated landslide or two\ncannot be ruled out.\n\n* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...\nLake Lure, Chimney Rock Village, Chimney Rock State Park, Bat Cave,\nGerton, and Shingle Hollow.",
                "instruction": "Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.\n\nThe additional heavy rain will increase the risk of landslides and\ndebris flows, especially in areas where landslides have occurred in\nthe past. Be especially alert if you live near a stream, particularly\nat the base of a mountain or in a cove. Watch for signs that a\nlandslide may be imminent, including loose-moving soil and rocks or a\nsudden increase in streamflow. Stay indoors and do NOT go outside to\ninvestigate. Escape vertically inside your home by moving upstairs or\ngetting on top of counters to avoid being swept away.",

                "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nFlorida...\n\nCypress Creek At SR 54 Worthington Gardens affecting Pasco County.\n\n...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...\n\nWithlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Levy and Citrus\nCounties.\n\n.Due to recent heavy rainfall, water levels on Cypress Creek remain\nelevated.                 "senderName": "NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL",
                "headline": "Flood Warning issued October 10 at 10:06PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL",
                "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nFlorida...\n\nCypress Creek At SR 54 Worthington Gardens affecting Pasco County.\n\n...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...\n\nWithlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Levy and Citrus\nCounties.\n\n.Due to recent heavy rainfall, water levels on Cypress Creek remain\nelevated. With additional heavy rainfall forecast, water levels are\nexpected to continue rising, and could reach minor flood stage in the\nnext few days.\n\nElevated water levels continue on the Withlacoochee River at\nDunnellon due to a combination of excessive hydrilla growth along a\n4.5 mile stretch of river between U.S. 41 and Lake Rousseau, and\nrecent heavy rainfall. Water levels are expected to hold steady\nbefore slowly decreasing over the next several days. However, the\nriver is forecast to remain in flood stage.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Cypress Creek at SR 54 Worthington Gardens.\n\n* WHEN...From late Monday night until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Flooding begins at the recreation area on\nState Road 54.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:00 PM EDT Saturday the stage was 7.0 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 8.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late\nMonday night and continue rising to 8.0 feet early Tuesday\nmorning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.\n- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 8.1\nfeet on 05/29/1976.\n- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
                "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads.                 "senderName": "NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC",
                "headline": "Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 9:43PM EDT until October 11 at 9:30AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC",
                "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Northern Greenville County in upstate South Carolina...\nNorthern Pickens County in upstate South Carolina...\n\n* WHEN...Until 930 AM EDT Sunday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams\nand other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,\ngreenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and\nparking lots.  Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.\nA few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A\nsmall culvert washout or two is possible.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 932 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a line of torrential\nrainfall quickly moving from south to north across northern\nPickens and Greenville counties.  This rainfall is occurring on\ntop of saturated soils due to a prolonged period of light to\nmoderate showers that have occurred over the county since this\nmorning.  Widespread, storm-total rainfall of the 2.5-3.5 inches\nhave fallen over the past 12 hours. The rainfall has accumulated\nsteadily, allowing soils to slowly saturate and runoff to slowly\nincrease, resulting in steady rises in small streams.  However,\nthis brief period of torrential rainfall is causing more rapid\nrises to develop, including along Eastatoe Creek near Rocky\nBottom and Sunset, Oolenoy River from Sunset to Pumpkintown,\nMiddle Saluda River from Jones Gap State Park to Cleveland, North\nSaluda River above the reservoir and below the reservoir near\nSlater- Marietta, and the headwaters of the South, Middle, and\nNorth Tyger rivers from Tigerville to Gowensville.  Isolated to\nscattered out-of-bank conditions impacting low-lying areas\nadjacent to streams are likely to develop over the next 1-3\nhours.\n\n- Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms may develop over\ntonight and the threat will persist through the early morning\nhours on Sunday.  These showers and storms will be very efficient\nat producing heavy rainfall.  Soils are saturated and streams are\nswollen. Therefore, additional heavy rain may quickly create new\nareas of flooding and cause previous areas of flooding to\nredevelop.  As a result, Flash Flood Warnings may be issued\ntonight.  Caution is advised near any stream or other vulnerable\narea.  Seek higher ground immediately if heavy rain develops.\nPlease have a plan in place should flash flooding develop and do\nnot hesitate to act.  Please heed all evacuation orders from\nEmergency Management officials.\n\n- Some locations that may experience flooding include...\nTravelers Rest, Slater-Marietta, Tryon, Pleasant Ridge State\nPark, Jones Gap State Park, Caesars Head State Park, Table Rock\nState Park, Tigerville, Jocassee Gorges, and Keowee Toxaway State\nPark.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
                "instruction": "Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.",

                "headline": "Flood Warning issued October 10 at 9:43PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL",
                "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...\n\nSt Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.\n\n.The St Johns River at Astor remains in Moderate Flood Stage due to\nrecent northeast winds and repeated rounds of heavy rainfall across\nthe basin.                 "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
                "senderName": "NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC",
                "headline": "Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 8:19PM EDT until October 11 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC",
                "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Spartanburg County in upstate South Carolina...\n\n* WHEN...Until 800 AM EDT Sunday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams\nand other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,\ngreenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and\nparking lots.  Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.\nA few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A\nsmall culvert washout or two is possible.\n\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 803 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a thunderstorm producing\ntorrential rainfall is quickly moving from south to north across\nthe county.  This torrential rainfall is occurring on top of\nsaturated soils due to a prolonged period of light to moderate\nshowers that have occurred over the county since this morning.\nWidespread, storm-total rainfall of the 2.5-3.5 inches have\nfallen over the past 12 hours. The rainfall has accumulated\nsteadily, allowing soils to slowly saturate and runoff to slowly\nincrease, resulting in steady rises in the small streams.\nHowever, this brief period of torrential rainfall is causing more\nrapid rises to develop, including along Lawsons Fork Creek from\nInman to Spartanburg, the South Pacolet River near Campobello,\nthe North Tyger River near Wellford and Lyman, and small\ntributaries to these rivers including Jordan Creek, Motlow Creek,\nand Meadow Creek.  Isolated out-of-bank conditions are likely to\ndevelop over the next 1-3 hours.\n\nGlendale Fire Department is reporting nuisance flooding along\nCountry Club Rd near Church St.  Please obey all barricades and\navoid flooded roadways.  Only a few inches of water can strand\nyour vehicle.\n\n- Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms may develop over\nthe next few hours and the threat will persist through the early\nmorning hours on Sunday.  These showers and storms will be very\nefficient at producing heavy rainfall.  Soils are saturated and\nstreams are swollen. Therefore, additional heavy rain may quickly\ncreate new areas of flooding and cause previous areas of flooding\nto redevelop.  As a result, Flash Flood Warnings may be issued\ntonight.  Caution is advised near any stream or other vulnerable\narea.  Seek higher ground immediately if heavy rain develops.\nPlease have a plan in place   should flash flooding develop and\ndo not hesitate to act.  Please heed all evacuation orders from\nEmergency Management officials.\n\n- Some locations that may experience flooding include...\nSpartanburg, Greer, Boiling Springs SC, Woodruff, Duncan, Lyman,\nPacolet, Landrum, Cowpens and Wellford.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
                "instruction": "Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.",
                "response": "Avoid",

                "description": "* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.4 ft of\ninundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas\nnear shorelines and tidal waterways.                 "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle\nCountry, Central Mountains, Eastern Juab/Millard Counties, San\nRafael Swell, Sanpete Valley, Sevier Valley, Wasatch Plateau/Book\nCliffs, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef National Park and\nVicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell, South Central\nUtah, Southern Mountains, Upper Sevier River Valleys, Western\nCanyonlands, Lower Washington County, Southwest Utah and Zion\nNational Park. This also includes recent burn scars such as\nForsyth, Cottonwood, Silver King, France Canyon, and Monroe Canyon.\n\n* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and\nflood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn\nscars. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may\noccur in poor drainage and urban areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Anomalously high moisture is forecast to impact the region with\nthe arrival of the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel. While this\nis expected to be a long duration rainfall event, scattered\ninstances of heavier rainfall rates are expected with stronger\nstorms yielding flash flooding concerns given saturated soils and\nprior burn scars.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

In addition,\nsignificant ponding of water on low-lying beach roadways could\nmake driving difficult. For all other beaches and harbors, shallow with\nminor to moderate sea- water flooding will likely impact\nbeaches and walkways, especially with the Sunday morning high\ntide which could cause local damage to most vulnerable locations\nsuch as Venice. For all beach areas, significant erosion is\nexpected. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning.\nDangerous and life- threatening rip currents can pull swimmers\nand surfers out to sea.                 "headline": "Flood Watch issued October 10 at 3:23PM EDT until October 11 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC",
                "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Most of coastal eastern North Carolina, including the\nfollowing areas, Coastal Onslow, East Carteret, Hatteras Island,\nInland Onslow, Jones, Mainland Dare, Mainland Hyde, Northern Outer\nBanks, Ocracoke Island, Pamlico, Southern Craven and West Carteret.\n\n* WHEN...Through Sunday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nFlooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- A plume of tropical moisture will overspread the area and will\ncombine with strong lift and weak to moderate instability to\nsupport areas of intense rainfall rates and an accompanying risk\nof flooding. Total rainfall of 3 to 5 inches are forecast, with\nlocally higher amounts possible. The highest amounts are expected\nto be where bands of thunderstorms are most persistent.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

                "instruction": "To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:\n\n* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are \"Unhealthy for\nSensitive Groups\" (orange), sensitive groups as specified\nabove should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.\n* When AQI is \"Unhealthy\" (red), everyone may experience health\nimpacts.                 "headline": "Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 10:57AM EDT until October 12 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC",
                "description": "...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in North\nCarolina...\n\nPigeon River At above Old River Rd (NC 215), 1 SW Canton affecting\nHaywood County.\n\n.Tropical rainfall will continue to overspread the mountains through\ntonight and become heavier. Storm-total rainfall of 4-8 inches is\nexpected, with isolated higher amounts possible across the upper\nPigeon River watershed upstream of Canton.  The highest totals will\noccur along the Pisgah ridge and in the Shining Rock and Middle Prong\nWilderness areas within the headwaters of the east and west forks of\nthe Pigeon River.  There remains enough confidence that  out-of-bank\nconditions are likely for the Pigeon River.  This rise above Action\nStage will result in nuisance, relatively shallow flooding of\nlow-lying areas adjacent to the Pigeon River, including farmland,\nwoodlands, low-lying secondary roads, greenways, parks, and other\nflood-prone locations.\n\nMore significant rises along the Pigeon River are possible, and those\nwith interests along the river are encouraged to stay weather aware\nand up-to-date on the latest stream levels and forecasts at\nhttps://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP.  Current reasonable worst-case\nscenarios are posted in the ADDITIONAL DETAILS sections below.\nForecast crests above Minor Flood Stage may result in the River Flood\nAdvisories being upgraded to River Flood Warnings.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.\n\n* WHERE...Pigeon River at above Old River Rd (NC 215), 1 SW Canton.\n\n* WHEN...Until late Sunday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Action/Advisory Stage.  Common, nuisance\nflooding of low-lying areas adjacent to the Pigeon River is\nbeginning.  Floodwaters are beginning to impact farmland,\nwoodlands, nurseries, parks, athletic fields, golf courses,\ngreenways, and boat-access areas with up to 2 feet of inundation.\nLow-water crossings may be inundated with up to 2 feet of\nfloodwater and become impassable.  Adjacent campgrounds, mobile\nhome/RV parks, and secondary roads may experience floodwater\ninundation of up to 1 foot.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 10:45 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 1.4 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.5 feet\ntomorrow morning.  The reasonable worst-case crest would be\naround the minor flood stage of 10 feet.\n- Action stage is 8.0 feet.\n- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
                "instruction": "Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.\n\nFor detailed information including observed and forecast stages,\nflood impacts, flood history, FEMA Flood Hazard Layers, and more,\nplease visit: https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP\n\nThe next statement should be issued late tonight before 500 AM EDT.",

                "description": "ESFGJT\n\nA strong low pressure system off the Pacific Coast will begin to draw\nin tropical moisture associated with Topical Storm Rachel this\nweekend. The chance for widespread precipitation\nincreases Saturday evening into Sunday. Total precipitation forecasts\nrange from 1 to 3 inches across high terrain, with highest amounts\nfavoring the Uintas, Tavaputs and the Southwest San Juan mountains.\n\nEmbedded thunderstorms are also possible Sunday afternoon, increasing\nthe threat for flash flooding across vulnerable terrain.
